title: A lint refuses a fixed sleep or wall-clock wait bound in a test
why: Owner 19:25 CST Nov 9: "against arbitrarily timed tests that have fixed values". Decision test-practices P5 (line 75) names this lint as owed and unbuilt. Main today: about 90 time.sleep calls across 12 test files (coordinator's git grep on origin/main), and hooks/test_session_start.py's watchdog case waits up to 10 s for a `sleep 7` process.
note: Scope: refuse a fixed sleep or a wall-clock wait bound in a test assert or wait (time.sleep(N), "sleep N" subprocesses, "up to N seconds" waits), with an exempt form for injected clocks. First lane: the lint, red on main, plus a list of offenders; re-pointing each offender is its own lane. One home: lint/find_time_pinned.py already lists fixed sleeps (step time-pinned-tests-go, #1026); extend it into the refusing lint before building a second. Related: convert-time-pinned-tests (doing, the 59 claude-settings sleeps), finder-deadline-poll (a poll in a deadline loop is not a fixed sleep: the exempt form should cover it), note session-start-watchdog-load. Filed 19:28 CST Nov 9 from the coordinator (19:27 CST). No owner question. Starts after convert-time-pinned-tests lands (coordinator 19:31 CST Nov 9): a refusing lint is red on main until those 59 sleeps are gone. Its brief names lint/find_time_pinned.py as the home to extend, and the finder-deadline-poll exempt form.
